data.title: Recycling lithium-ion batteries from electric vehicles | Nature
Recycling lithium-ion batteries from electric vehicles

passages.title: Recycling of critical minerals - IEA
passages.text:
Recycling can relieve pressure on primary supply of critical minerals. For batteries, the volume of spent electric vehicle packs remains small before 2030, but it grows rapidly afterwards.

Battery recycling capacity

Global battery recycling capacity exceeded 1.6 million tonnes per year in 2023, with the large majority located in China. Announced projects in Europe and North America would expand capacity further, though many plants currently process manufacturing scrap rather than end-of-life batteries.

passages.title: Battery recycling - Wikipedia
passages.text:
Battery recycling is a recycling activity that aims to reduce the number of batteries being disposed of as municipal solid waste. Batteries contain a number of heavy metals and toxic chemicals, and disposing of them by the same process as regular household waste has raised concerns over soil contamination and water pollution.

Lead-acid batteries

Lead-acid batteries are the most recycled consumer product. In the United States the recycling rate of lead-acid batteries is about 99 percent. The batteries are broken apart in a hammer mill, the lead grids and paste are smelted, and the polypropylene cases are washed and turned into pellets for new cases. The sulfuric acid is neutralised or converted to sodium sulfate for use in detergent and glass manufacture.

passages.title: Battery recycling - Wikipedia
passages.text:
Collection

Collection is the main obstacle to battery recycling. Small batteries are often thrown away with household waste, where they can start fires in waste trucks and sorting plants. Many countries require retailers to take back used batteries, and the European Union battery regulation sets collection targets for portable batteries of 63 percent by 2027 and 73 percent by 2030.

Second life

Electric vehicle batteries that no longer meet vehicle requirements usually retain 70 to 80 percent of their capacity. Before recycling, such packs can be reused in stationary energy storage, which extends their useful life by several years.

passages.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Recycling | US EPA
passages.text:
Lithium-ion batteries power devices such as mobile phones, laptops, power tools and electric vehicles. When they are damaged or improperly disposed of, they can cause fires during transport and at recycling and waste facilities.

Why recycle lithium-ion batteries

Recycling lithium-ion batteries conserves critical minerals such as cobalt, lithium and nickel, reduces the environmental impact of mining, and prevents fires caused by batteries placed in household trash or curbside recycling bins.

How to recycle

Do not put lithium-ion batteries in the trash or in municipal recycling bins. Take them to separate recycling or household hazardous waste collection points. Many retailers that sell rechargeable batteries offer free drop-off. Tape the terminals or place each battery in a separate plastic bag to prevent short circuits.

Damaged, defective or recalled batteries need special handling; contact the manufacturer or the local waste authority before transporting them.

Regulations

Most lithium-ion batteries are managed under the universal waste regulations, which simplify collection and transport for businesses. Batteries that are sent for recycling are counted as universal waste until they reach the destination facility. EPA is developing best management practices for battery collection, sorting and transport as required by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

passages.title: Battery recycling - Wikipedia
passages.text:
Lithium-ion batteries contain cobalt, nickel, manganese, lithium, copper and aluminium. Only a small share of lithium-ion batteries were recycled in the 2010s, although the rate is rising as electric vehicle packs reach the end of their life. Recycling recovers valuable metals and reduces the need for new mining.

The main industrial routes are pyrometallurgy, where cells are smelted and cobalt, nickel and copper are recovered as an alloy, and hydrometallurgy, where the black mass obtained by shredding is leached in acid and the metals are separated by solvent extraction and precipitation. Lithium is lost to the slag in most smelting processes, which is one reason hydrometallurgical plants have grown.

passages.title: Field notes: battery collection pilot
passages.text:
Summary

The municipal pilot collected 4.2 tonnes of portable batteries in six months from 38 drop-off points. Lithium-ion cells made up 31 percent of the weight, and 12 swollen or damaged cells were set aside for special handling.

Costs

Transport to the recycler was the largest cost item. Sorting by chemistry before shipment reduced the gate fee charged for mixed loads.

passages.title: Recycling lithium-ion batteries from electric vehicles
passages.text:
Gavin Harper, Roberto Sommerville, Emma Kendrick, et al.

Abstract. Rapid growth in the market for electric vehicles is imperative to meet global targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The resulting volume of spent lithium-ion batteries presents both a waste management challenge and an opportunity to recover valuable materials. Here we outline the approaches available to recycle the batteries and the research needed to make the recycling of electric vehicle batteries economic.

A single electric vehicle pack can weigh more than 250 kg and contain hundreds of cells. Disassembly is labour intensive and hazardous because packs can retain high voltage. Automated disassembly and design for recycling would lower costs.

Pyrometallurgical recycling smelts whole cells or modules. It is robust to variations in chemistry but consumes much energy and loses lithium and aluminium to the slag. Hydrometallurgical recycling leaches shredded black mass in acid and recovers high purity cobalt, nickel, manganese and lithium salts, at the cost of large volumes of reagents and effluent. Direct recycling recovers the cathode material and relithiates it without breaking it down to elements, which preserves the value added during cathode manufacture.

The economics of recycling depend strongly on cathode chemistry. Cobalt-rich chemistries carry the most value, while lithium iron phosphate cells contain little that is worth recovering by conventional routes. Transport of spent packs, classified as dangerous goods, can account for a large share of the recycling cost.

Standardised pack designs, labelling of cell chemistry and policy measures such as recycled content requirements would make battery recycling more efficient and less costly.

passages.title: Recycling of critical minerals - IEA
passages.text:
Costs and revenues

The profitability of a battery recycling plant depends on metal prices, the chemistry of the incoming batteries and the cost of collection and transport. When lithium and cobalt prices fell in 2023, margins for recyclers dropped sharply. Gate fees charged for low value chemistries help keep plants economic.

Policy

Extended producer responsibility, minimum recycled content and recovery efficiency targets, such as those in the European Union battery regulation, give recyclers more certainty about feedstock and demand. Recycled supply could meet a meaningful share of lithium, nickel and cobalt demand by 2040 if collection rates improve.
